1	/-

     5	-/
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AtlasFromDivRepAffChallenge
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Application formulas for the admissible widened Abel map
    10	
    11	This file isolates the map-level equalities needed after a widened divisor family has been
    12	constructed on an affine test. It exposes the chart datum chosen inside the admissible map,
    13	computes a represented point under the Sigma-extended Abel transformation, identifies the
    14	affine Abel value after the vehicle collapse, and packages the final cancellation of the
    15	fixed chart twists.
    16	
    17	No quotient, atlas, or representability conclusion is asserted here.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	set_option autoImplicit false
    21	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    22	
    23	universe u
    24	
    25	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
    26	
    27	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    28	
    29	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    30	
    31	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    32	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    33	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    34	
    35	noncomputable section
    36	
    37	variable (C) in
    38	/-- The chart index and divisor chosen inside the admissible Abel map can be exposed without
    39	choosing new data. The equality is definitional after unfolding the admissible map. -/
    40	theorem exists_abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible_eq :
    41	    ∃ (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    42	      (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
    43	        = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)
    44	          - (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C : ℤ)),
    45	      abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C =
    46	        abelSigmaChartAff C (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C)
    47	          (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C) m Z hdeg := by
    48	  dsimp only [abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible]
    49	  exact ⟨_, _, _, rfl⟩
    50	
    51	variable {n : ℕ}
    52	
    53	/-- Classifying a section with a representer and then evaluating the Sigma-extended Abel map
    54	at the underlying scheme morphism returns the original section's chart value. The equality of
    55	the two structure morphisms is handled by sigma-extension extensionality. -/
    56	theorem abelSigmaChartAff_app_homEquiv_symm
    57	    {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    58	    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D)
    59	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    60	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
    61	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
    62	    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (a : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    63	    (s : divFamZarAff C n (Over.mk a)) :
    64	    let q := rep.homEquiv.symm s
    65	    (abelSigmaChartAff C n rep m Z hdeg).app (op Y) q.left =
    66	      (⟨a, (chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).app (op (Over.mk a)) s⟩ :
    67	        (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) := by
    68	  let q := rep.homEquiv.symm s
    69	  change (abelSigmaChartAff C n rep m Z hdeg).app (op Y) q.left =
    70	    (⟨a, (chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).app (op (Over.mk a)) s⟩ :
    71	      (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y))
    72	  change (⟨q.left ≫ D.hom, _⟩ :
    73	      (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) =
    74	    ⟨a, (chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).app (op (Over.mk a)) s⟩
    75	  refine Over.sigmaExtension_ext (pic0TypeFunctor C) q.w ?_
    76	  let e := Over.mkCongr q.w
    77	  let q' : Over.mk (q.left ≫ D.hom) ⟶ D :=
    78	    Over.homMk (U := Over.mk (q.left ≫ D.hom)) q.left
    79	  change (pic0TypeFunctor C).map e.op
    80	      ((chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).app (op (Over.mk a)) s) =
    81	    (chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).app
    82	      (op (Over.mk (q.left ≫ D.hom))) (rep.homEquiv q')
    83	  have hhom : e ≫ q = q' := by
    84	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
    85	    exact Category.id_comp _
    86	  have hq : rep.homEquiv q = s := by
    87	    dsimp only [q]
    88	    exact Equiv.apply_symm_apply rep.homEquiv s
    89	  have hfamily : rep.homEquiv q' =
    90	      (divFunctorAff C n).map e.op s := by
    91	    calc
    92	      rep.homEquiv q' = rep.homEquiv (e ≫ q) := congrArg rep.homEquiv hhom.symm
    93	      _ = (divFunctorAff C n).map e.op (rep.homEquiv q) := rep.homEquiv_comp e q
    94	      _ = (divFunctorAff C n).map e.op s := congrArg _ hq
    95	  have hnat := ConcreteCategory.congr_hom
    96	    ((chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).naturality e.op) s
    97	  calc
    98	    _ = (chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).app
    99	        (op (Over.mk (q.left ≫ D.hom))) ((divFunctorAff C n).map e.op s) := by
   100	      simpa only [ConcreteCategory.comp_apply] using hnat.symm
   101	    _ = _ := congrArg _ hfamily.symm
   102	
   103	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
   104	/-- On an affine test, passing a widened affine family through the inverse vehicle comparison
   105	and then taking its Abel value recovers the direct affine Abel value. -/
   106	theorem picEtAffineEquiv_abelDivAff'_affineEquiv_symm
   107	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (F : DivFamZarAff C A n) :
   108	    picEtAffineEquiv C A
   109	        (abelDivAff' C n (overSpec k A) ((divFamZarAffAffineEquiv C n A).symm F))
   110	      = abelDivAffPlus C A F := by
   111	  rw [picEtAffineEquiv_abelDivAff', Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
   112	
   113	/-- If the Abel value of a widened family is the inverse chart twist of a target degree-zero
   114	class, then the chart transformation sends that family to the target itself. -/
   115	theorem chartValueAffTrans_app_eq_of_abelDivAff'_eq_chartTwist
   116	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   117	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   118	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   119	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (s : divFamZarAff C n T)
   120	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T)
   121	    (habel : abelDivAff' C n T s = chartTwist C m Z T lam.1) :
   122	    (chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).app (op T) s = lam := by
   123	  apply Subtype.ext
   124	  rw [chartValueAffTrans_app_coe]
   125	  change chartValueAff C n m Z T s = lam.1
   126	  rw [chartValueAff, habel, chartTwist]
   127	  group
   128	
   129	end
   130	
   131	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-
     2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoverageAffineTest
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartHonest
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Etale-site reduction and affine PicEt honestification
    11	
    12	This file provides the site-theoretic and affine-plus infrastructure used to turn affine
    13	local lifts into local surjectivity on the big etale site. It also packages the passage from
    14	an affine `picEt` class to an honest relative Picard class after restriction to the carrier of
    15	one of its etale presentations.
    16	
    17	The declarations here are independent of the Abel transformation and make no representability
    18	or quotient assertion.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	set_option autoImplicit false
    22	
    23	universe u
    24	
    25	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    26	
    27	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    28	
    29	noncomputable section
    30	
    31	/-! ## Reduction to affine tests -/
    32	
    33	/-- A sieve on a scheme is etale-covering if its pullback to every member of the canonical
    34	affine open cover is etale-covering. -/
    35	theorem mem_etaleTopology_of_pullback_affine {T : Scheme.{u}} (S : Sieve T)
    36	    (h : ∀ (j : T.affineCover.I₀), S.pullback (T.affineCover.f j) ∈
    37	      Scheme.etaleTopology (T.affineCover.X j)) :
    38	    S ∈ Scheme.etaleTopology T := by
    39	  have hcov : (Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows T.affineCover.X T.affineCover.f))
    40	      ∈ Scheme.etaleTopology T := by
    41	    apply Scheme.zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology
    42	    exact Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
    43	      ⟨T.affineCover, Sieve.le_generate _⟩
    44	  refine Scheme.etaleTopology.transitive hcov S ?_
    45	  rintro Y g ⟨V, a, b, ⟨j⟩, rfl⟩
    46	  rw [Sieve.pullback_comp]
    47	  exact Scheme.etaleTopology.pullback_stable a (h j)
    48	
    49	/-- To prove local surjectivity on the big etale site, it suffices to produce an etale cover
    50	with local lifts over every affine test scheme. -/
    51	theorem isLocallySurjective_etale_of_affine
    52	    {F G : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : F ⟶ G)
    53	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : G.obj (op Y)),
    54	      ∃ (cover : Y.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @Etale)),
    55	        ∀ j : cover.I₀, ∃ x : F.obj (op (cover.X j)),
    56	          f.app (op (cover.X j)) x = G.map (cover.f j).op s) :
    57	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.etaleTopology f where
    58	  imageSieve_mem {U} s := by
    59	    apply mem_etaleTopology_of_pullback_affine
    60	    intro j
    61	    rw [Presheaf.pullback_imageSieve]
    62	    obtain ⟨cover, hcover⟩ :=
    63	      h (U.affineCover.X j) (G.map (U.affineCover.f j).op s)
    64	    refine (Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff (P := @Etale)).mpr ⟨cover, ?_⟩
    65	    rintro Y g ⟨i⟩
    66	    exact hcover i
    67	
    68	/-! ## Covers induced by affine etale presentations -/
    69	
    70	/-- The spectrum of the carrier of an algebraic etale cover is a singleton etale cover of
    71	the spectrum of the base algebra. -/
    72	noncomputable def etaleSchemeCover {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    73	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
    74	    (Spec (.of A)).Cover (Scheme.precoverage @Etale) :=
    75	  Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers PUnit (fun _ => Spec (.of E.Carrier))
    76	    (fun _ => Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)))
    77	    (fun x => by
    78	      obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := E.comap_surjective x
    79	      exact ⟨PUnit.unit, y, hy⟩)
    80	    (fun _ => by
    81	      rw [HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff (P := @Etale)]
    82	      exact RingHom.etale_algebraMap.mpr inferInstance)
    83	
    84	/-! ## Honestification of affine PicEt classes -/
    85	
    86	namespace PicEtAff
    87	
    88	/-- `mapAlg` agrees with the instance-based affine restriction map when the underlying ring
    89	homomorphism is the chosen `A`-algebra structure on `B`. -/
    90	theorem mapAlg_eq_map_of_toRingHom_eq_algebraMap
    91	    {k A B : Type u} [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B]
    92	    [Algebra k B] [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower k A B]
    93	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (phi : A →ₐ[k] B)
    94	    (hphi : phi.toRingHom = algebraMap A B) (a : PicEtAff C A) :
    95	    PicEtAff.mapAlg C phi a = PicEtAff.map C B a := by
    96	  have hAlg : phi.toRingHom.toAlgebra = (inferInstance : Algebra A B) :=
    97	    Algebra.algebra_ext _ _ fun r => by
    98	      change phi r = algebraMap A B r
    99	      exact DFunLike.congr_fun hphi r
   100	  unfold PicEtAff.mapAlg
   101	  subst hAlg
   102	  rfl
   103	
   104	/-- Restricting an affine PicEt presentation along the map to its own cover carrier produces
   105	the honest class represented by its descent datum. -/
   106	theorem mapAlg_mk_eq_unit_self
   107	    {k A : Type u} [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   108	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   109	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) :
   110	    PicEtAff.mapAlg C ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)
   111	        (PicEtAff.mk C E x)
   112	      = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier
   113	          (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) := by
   114	  rw [mapAlg_eq_map_of_toRingHom_eq_algebraMap C _ rfl]
   115	  exact PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self C E x
   116	
   117	end PicEtAff
   118	
   119	/-- On affine tests, restricting a `picEt` class to the carrier of one of its plus
   120	presentations agrees with the `picEt` unit of the corresponding honest relative Picard
   121	class. -/
   122	theorem picEtMap_eq_relPicToPicEt_of_affineRepresentative
   123	    {k A : Type u} [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   124	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   125	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
   126	    (lam : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A)
   127	    (x : descentClasses C E)
   128	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C A lam = PicEtAff.mk C E x) :
   129	    picEtMap C
   130	        (Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)) lam
   131	      = relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier)
   132	          (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) := by
   133	  apply (picEtAffineEquiv C E.Carrier).injective
   134	  rw [picEtAffineEquiv_naturality, h,
   135	    picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt,
   136	    PicEtAff.mapAlg_mk_eq_unit_self]
   137	
   138	end
   139	
   140	end AlgebraicGeometry

/-- Multiplication-injectivity on a residue fibre is the pure-tensor nonzerodivisor
condition for a component of a cocycle-datum section. -/
theorem component_tmul_one_mem_nonZeroDivisors
    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    letI : Algebra B Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) :=
      ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B (D.pieces j)).toAlgebra
    (D.component s j ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
      Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
        nonZeroDivisors
          (Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
  letI : Algebra B Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) :=
    ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B (D.pieces j)).toAlgebra
  have hend : Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j) =
      LinearMap.mulLeft B (D.component s j) := by
    ext t
    simp [Scheme.mulSectionEnd_apply]
  have hinj := hfib j p
  rw [hend, rTensor_mulLeft_eq_mulLeft_tmul p.asIdeal.ResidueField
    (D.component s j)] at hinj
  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff]
  constructor
  · intro z hz
    apply hinj
    rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mul_zero]
    exact hz
  · intro z hz
    apply hinj
    rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mul_zero, mul_comm]
    exact hz

omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] in
/-- A fibrewise-regular component remains a nonzerodivisor after arbitrary coefficient
extension, read through the section ring of its affine open. -/

(relCurve C B).basicOpen (D.toBasicOpenCoverData.pinnedGenerator j))
  | Sum.inl j => D.component s (Sum.inl j)
  | Sum.inr j => D.component s (Sum.inr j)

/-- Fibrewise injectivity of multiplication by a datum component gives the ring-theoretic
nonzerodivisor condition on its pure tensor. -/
theorem component_tmul_one_mem_nonZeroDivisors
    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    letI : Algebra B Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) :=
      ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B (D.pieces j)).toAlgebra
    (D.component s j ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
      Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
        nonZeroDivisors
          (Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
  letI : Algebra B Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) :=
    ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B (D.pieces j)).toAlgebra
  have hend : Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j) =
      LinearMap.mulLeft B (D.component s j) := by
    ext t
    simp [Scheme.mulSectionEnd_apply]
  have hinj := hfib j p
  rw [hend, rTensor_mulLeft_eq_mulLeft_tmul p.asIdeal.ResidueField
    (D.component s j)] at hinj
  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff]
  constructor
  · intro z hz
    apply hinj
    rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mul_zero]
    exact hz
  · intro z hz
    apply hinj
    rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mul_zero, mul_comm]
    exact hz

/-- Fibrewise-regular datum components remain nonzerodivisors on their pinned basic opens

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",
